messages.author: 3bb66fbd2ed88a1d
messages.subject: Re: How to declare a vectors of pointers to ggplot graphs?
parts:
How cool is this? I can then just say to print q!

-Mary

--- mfcov...@gmail.com wrote:

From: Mike Covington <mfcov...@gmail.com>
To: ggp...@googlegroups.com
Cc: mlho...@avalon.net
Subject: Re: How to declare a vectors of pointers to ggplot graphs?
Date: Tue, 5 Feb 2013 16:27:41 -0800 (PST)

This is really cool. While messing with this, I found that you can simplify
how you point to the plots in saveHTML(). Given a list of ggplot objects, q,
the following outputs the same as the for loop approach:

saveHTML(q,
img.name = "test",
single.opts = "'utf8': false",
autoplay = FALSE,
interval = 0.5,
imgdir = "claimsplot_dir",
htmlfile = "test.html",
ani.height = 600,
ani.width = 800,
title = "Test",
outdir=getwd())

I left everything except the first argument the same as what you had.


On Monday, February 4, 2013 9:45:49 AM UTC-8, Mary wrote:
>
> That's great! Then I don't have to know in advance how many graphs I will
> have in my slide show.
>
> -Mary
>
> --- ista...@gmail.com <javascript:> wrote:
>
> From: Ista Zahn <ista...@gmail.com <javascript:>>
> To: mlho...@avalon.net <javascript:>
> Cc: ggp...@googlegroups.com <javascript:>
> Subject: Re: How to declare a vectors of pointers to ggplot graphs?
> Date: Mon, 4 Feb 2013 12:26:28 -0500
>
> On Mon, Feb 4, 2013 at 12:09 PM, Mary <mlho...@avalon.net <javascript:>>
> wrote:
> > Thanks so much to Ista and Dennis and everyone who contributed!
>
> You are welcome! Just one quick clarification below.
>
> >
> >
> > Now I can test out my plots such as this:
> >
> > q <- list(27)
>
> The 27 is not needed, and will just be overwritten later. Just do
>
> q <- list()
>
> or, if you really must pre-allocate the length at 27, do
>
> q <- vector("list", 27)
>
> >
> > p <- ggplot(...)
> > q[[1]] <- p
> >
> >
> > And then in the animation I can play them back like this:
> >
> > library(animation)
> > saveHTML(
> > {
> > for (i in 1:27)
> > {
> > print(q[[i]])
> > }
> > }
> > , img.name = "test", single.opts = "'utf8': false", autoplay = FALSE,
> > interval = 0.5, imgdir = "claimsplot_dir", htmlfile = "test.html",
> > ani.height = 600, ani.width = 800, title = "Test",
> > outdir=getwd())
> >
> >
> > -Mary
> >
> > p.s. I think I also learned a lot about R in the lively discussion. I
> think the most important point was that when we assign a graph to a
> variable like p, we are saving the instructions on how to create the graph
> rather than the graph itself. So they are not pointers, but rather they
> are lists with the information needed to create the graph.
> >
